timeline.title: National Computer Board Established
timeline.description: The National Computer Board was established on 1 September 1981 to spearhead Singapore's computerisation and launched the Civil Service Computerisation Programme.
timeline.significance: Marked the beginning of Singapore's digital transformation journey.

timeline.title: NUS Connects to BITNET
timeline.description: In January 1987, NUS became the first permanent BITNET node in Southeast Asia outside Japan, connecting to over 600 universities worldwide.
timeline.significance: Put Singapore on the international academic networking map.

timeline.title: NUS Achieves First Internet Connection
timeline.description: NUS achieved Singapore's first full connection to the global Internet.
timeline.significance: Singapore joined the global Internet community.

timeline.title: NUSNET Officially Launched
timeline.description: On 11 April 1991, NUSNET was launched — a campus-wide fibre network connecting NUS to more than 3,000 institutions worldwide.
timeline.significance: Established one of the most advanced academic networks in Asia.

timeline.title: TechNet Established
timeline.description: The National Science and Technology Board established TechNet as Singapore's first Internet service provider.
timeline.significance: Singapore's first ISP laid the groundwork for commercial Internet.

timeline.title: IT2000 Masterplan Adopted
timeline.description: The IT2000 masterplan was adopted by the Singapore Cabinet, envisioning an 'Intelligent Island'.
timeline.significance: First comprehensive national blueprint for Singapore's IT future.

timeline.title: SingNet Launched
timeline.description: In July 1994, Singtel launched SingNet — Singapore's first commercial ISP.
timeline.significance: Democratised Internet access for millions of Singaporeans.

timeline.title: Pacific Internet Formed
timeline.description: Sembawang Media purchased TechNet and formed Pacific Internet, later the first Asian ISP to list on NASDAQ.
timeline.significance: Demonstrated commercial viability of Internet services in Singapore.

timeline.title: Cyberway Begins Operations
timeline.description: Cyberway launched as Singapore's third major ISP, later acquired by StarHub in 1999.
timeline.significance: Increased competition and expanded consumer choice.

timeline.title: Singapore ONE Launched
timeline.description: On 9 June 1997, PM Goh Chok Tong launched Singapore ONE — the world's first nationwide broadband network.
timeline.significance: Pioneered residential broadband and digital services.

timeline.title: Infocomm 21 Masterplan Launched
timeline.description: Launched in December 2000, Infocomm 21 set a five-year vision to transform Singapore into a global Infocomm Capital.
timeline.significance: Established Singapore's ambition to become a global technology hub.

timeline.title: Singpass Launched
timeline.description: In March 2003, Singapore launched Singpass — the national digital identity system.
timeline.significance: Revolutionised government service delivery.

timeline.title: iN2015 Masterplan Launched
timeline.description: In June 2006, Singapore launched iN2015 — a S$3.2 billion, 10-year masterplan.
timeline.significance: Prepared Singapore for the digital age.

timeline.title: Wireless@SG Launched
timeline.description: In December 2006, Singapore launched Wireless@SG — one of the first nationwide free Wi-Fi networks.
timeline.significance: Promoted a connected lifestyle in Singapore.

timeline.title: Next Generation NBN Launched
timeline.description: In August 2010, Singapore's Next Generation National Broadband Network began commercial operations with 1 Gbps speeds.
timeline.significance: Singapore joined global leaders in broadband connectivity.

timeline.title: Smart Nation Vision Launched
timeline.description: On 24 November 2014, PM Lee Hsien Loong launched the Smart Nation vision.
timeline.significance: Singapore's most ambitious digital transformation strategy.

timeline.title: GovTech Formed
timeline.description: In October 2016, the Government Technology Agency was established.
timeline.significance: Created a dedicated agency for government digital transformation.

timeline.title: SNDGO Established
timeline.description: On 1 May 2017, the Smart Nation and Digital Government Office was established under the PMO.
timeline.significance: Centralised Smart Nation strategy and decision-making.

timeline.title: PayNow Launched
timeline.description: On 10 July 2017, Singapore launched PayNow — an instant peer-to-peer fund transfer system.
timeline.significance: Revolutionised digital payments in Singapore.

timeline.title: National AI Strategy Unveiled
timeline.description: On 13 November 2019, Singapore unveiled its National AI Strategy 1.0.
timeline.significance: Positioned Singapore as a global AI leader.

timeline.title: 5G Licences Awarded
timeline.description: In June 2020, Singapore awarded 5G licences to Singtel and a StarHub-M1 joint venture.
timeline.significance: Began nationwide 5G rollout for IoT and smart city services.

timeline.title: Smart Nation 2.0 Launched
timeline.description: On 1 October 2024, PM Lawrence Wong launched Smart Nation 2.0 — Trust, Growth, Community.
timeline.significance: Next phase of digital transformation with human-centric focus.
